text.text: The parent-report Children's Obsessional Compulsive Inventory–Revised (ChOCI-R-P) was
The respondent rated the child at 25 out of a possible 40 on Total Symptoms,
placing the child at the 80th percentile. The child's symptoms are considered moderate for
children with OCD. This reflected moderate obsessions (12/20) and moderate compulsions
(13/20). In particular, the respondent endorsed the following items:
- 1. They spend far too much time washing their hands over and over again. (A lot)
- 2. They feel they must do ordinary/everyday things exactly the same way, every time they do
The respondent rated the child at 23 out of a possible 48 on Total Impairment,
placing the child at the 14th percentile. The child's functional impairment is considered mild for
The respondent's open-text descriptions of the child's habits (items 11 to 13) and thoughts
(items 30 to 32) appear in the Client Responses section and may guide formulation.
For comprehensive information on the ChOCI-R-P,
The Children's Obsessional Compulsive Inventory–Revised – Parent Report (ChOCI-R-P)
results in six raw scores which are computed by summing item responses. Higher values
indicate greater OCD severity. The ChOCI-R-P measures both symptoms and impairment:
- Total Symptoms (sum of Compulsion Symptoms and Obsession Symptoms; scores range from
- Compulsion Symptoms (items 1 to 10; scores range from 0 to 20): sum of 10 items
- Obsession Symptoms (items 20 to 29; scores range from 0 to 20): sum of 10 items
- Total Impairment (sum of Compulsion Impairment and Obsession Impairment; scores range
- Compulsion Impairment (items 14 to 19; scores range from 0 to 24): sum of 6 items
- Obsession Impairment (items 33 to 38; scores range from 0 to 24): sum of 6 items
Three open-text items in each of the symptom sections (items 11 to 13 for habits and items 30 to
32 for thoughts) ask the parent to describe the child's three most upsetting habits and thoughts.
These items are not included in the scoring, but provide more detail of the habits and thoughts to
Each raw score is presented with a percentile rank against an OCD-clinical reference sample. A
percentile of 50 corresponds to the OCD-clinical reference average; a percentile of 80 indicates
a score exceeding approximately 80% of OCD-diagnosed children in the reference group.
Each of the six scores is reported with a severity descriptor alongside its percentile.
A Low label (green) indicates a symptom level lower than typical for children with OCD
(atypically light for this reference group); Moderate (yellow) indicates a symptom level within the
typical range for children with OCD; High (red) indicates a symptom level above the typical OCD-
clinical range. Each subscale has its own cut-offs, placed at the same position in the reference
sample as the Total Symptoms cut-offs:
A Minimal label (white) indicates functional disruption lower than typical for children with OCD;
Mild (green) indicates mild functional disruption relative to the OCD-clinical reference; Moderate
(yellow) indicates functional disruption within the typical OCD-clinical range; Severe (orange)
indicates functional disruption above the typical OCD-clinical level (substantial day-to-day
interference); Extreme (red) indicates functional disruption at the top of the OCD-clinical
distribution (pervasive disruption). Each subscale has its own cut-offs, placed at the same
position in the reference sample as the Total Impairment cut-offs:
Each ChOCI-R-P subscale captures a clinically distinct dimension of OCD presentation. Higher
scores on Compulsion Symptoms indicate that the parent has observed more frequent or more
severe compulsive behaviours, including washing, checking, ordering, counting, repeating, and
reassurance-seeking. Higher scores on Obsession Symptoms indicate more frequent intrusive
thoughts of harm, contamination, doubt, mortality, blasphemy, or aggressive content. Higher
scores on Compulsion Impairment indicate greater functional disruption from compulsions,
including time spent, interference with school and friends, distress when prevented from acting,
weak resistance, low control, and avoidance. Higher scores on Obsession Impairment indicate
When the ChOCI-R-P is administered on multiple occasions, change between administrations is
interpreted via a Reliable Change Index (RCI). A change of approximately 8.4 raw-score points
or greater on Total Impairment or 8.6 or greater on Total Symptoms, is interpreted as a reliable
On first administration, the report presents a results table followed by two construct sections
(Symptoms and Impairment). Each section contains two horizontal raw-score charts. The first
plots the construct's total as a single bar with the client's raw score on a 0–40 axis for Symptoms
or 0–48 for Impairment. A clinical 25th-to-75th percentile reference rectangle and a dashed line
at the clinical average show the score relative to the clinical reference sample of children with
OCD. The second plots the construct's two subscales (Compulsion and Obsession bars on a
0–20 axis for Symptoms or 0–24 for Impairment, each with its own 25th-to-75th reference
rectangle and clinical-average line). Beneath each bar, a coloured strip marks that scale's
descriptor bands (Low, Moderate and High for Symptoms; Minimal, Mild, Moderate, Severe and
Extreme for Impairment, with Minimal shown in white).
On repeat administration, the report presents the same results table followed by a 2×3 grid of
multi-administration raw-score line plots organised by construct: top row Symptoms (Total,
Compulsions, Obsessions); bottom row Impairment (Total, Compulsions, Obsessions). Each plot
shows one score over time on its own descriptor bands, so the shading behind each point
matches that score's descriptor in the results table.
